text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Lars Sponheim, member of parliament for the liberal Venstre party, admits that the centre parties showed little moderation in this year's budget talks. Sponheim says Venstre in a possible government coalition made up of the three centrist parties would seek to hold back on spending.
-Norwegian authorities have decided that the passengers on board the luxury liner Hanseatic will be evacuated today. The ship ran aground off the Arctic island of Spitzbergen on Sunday.
-Only one percent of Norwegian farmers grow ecological products. However increasing demand for "green" foodstuff is expected to boost interest in such farming.
-Norwegian politicians see nothing dramatic in yesterday's raise in interest rates. The central bank said on Wednesday it had decided to raise official rates by 25 points.

-Finance minister Jens Stoltenberg says the government and the central bank agreed that a raise in deposit rates was necessary in order to strenghten the Norwegian crown. However Stoltenberg declines to comment on whether he sees the 25 point hike as sufficient to secure stable exchange rates.

-Knut A. Mork, chief economist at Handelsbanken, belives that the central bank raised deposit rates by 25 points instead of 50 points because of pressure from the government. The ruling Labour party has garanteed voters in the campaign for the September election that there will be no dramatic raise in rates.
